nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a measurable space in which every singleton is measurable, let $\delta_{x_0}$ be the Dirac measure at a point $x_0 \in X$, and let $s \subseteq X$ be a set with $x_0 \notin s$. Then for every natural number $n \ge 1$, $\frac{1}{n} \log \delta_{x_0}(s) = -\infty$ in the extended reals, with $\log 0 = -\infty$.
nodes.title: Log-scaled Dirac mass of a set avoiding the center

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a measurable space, let $\delta_{x_0}$ be the Dirac measure at a point $x_0 \in X$, and let $s \subseteq X$ be a set with $x_0 \in s$. Then $\frac{1}{n} \log \delta_{x_0}(s) = 0$ in the extended reals for every natural number $n$, the factor $1/n$ being read as $0$ when $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Log-scaled Dirac mass of a set containing the center

nodes.summary: For points $x \ne x_0$ of a set $X$, the Dirac rate function at $x_0$ takes the value $\infty$ at $x$.
nodes.title: The Dirac rate function is infinite away from its center

nodes.summary: For every point $x_0$ of a set $X$, the Dirac rate function at $x_0$ takes the value $0$ at $x_0$.
nodes.title: The Dirac rate function vanishes at its center

nodes.summary: For a point $x_0$ of a set $X$, the Dirac rate function at $x_0$ is the function $X \to [0, \infty]$ that equals $0$ at $x_0$ and $\infty$ at every other point.
nodes.title: Rate function of a Dirac mass

nodes.summary: For a point $x_0$ of a set $X$ and a subset $s \subseteq X$ with $x_0 \in s$, the infimum over $x \in s$ of the Dirac rate function at $x_0$, evaluated at $x$, is $0$.
nodes.title: Infimum of the Dirac rate function over a set containing the center

nodes.summary: For a point $x_0$ of a set $X$ and a subset $s \subseteq X$ with $x_0 \notin s$, the infimum over $x \in s$ of the Dirac rate function at $x_0$, evaluated at $x$, is $\infty$.
nodes.title: Infimum of the Dirac rate function over a set avoiding the center

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a real vector space carrying a topology (no compatibility between the topology and the linear structure is assumed). A function $I : X \to [0, \infty]$ is a convex rate function if it is a rate function and $I(ax + by) \le a I(x) + b I(y)$ for all $x, y \in X$ and all real numbers $a, b \ge 0$ with $a + b = 1$.
nodes.title: Convex rate function

nodes.summary: The function $x \mapsto |x|$, viewed as a map $\mathbb{R} \to [0, \infty]$, is a good rate function on $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: The absolute value is a good rate function

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a topological space. A function $I : X \to [0, \infty]$ is a good rate function if it is a rate function and, for every real number $a \ge 0$, the sub-level set $\{x \in X : I(x) \le a\}$ is compact.
nodes.title: Good rate function

nodes.summary: Every good rate function on a topological space is a rate function.
nodes.title: Good rate functions are rate functions

nodes.summary: Every convex rate function on a real vector space with a topology is a rate function.
nodes.title: Convex rate functions are rate functions

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a topological space. A rate function on $X$ is a lower semicontinuous function $I : X \to [0, \infty]$.
nodes.title: Rate function

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a $T_1$ topological space equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and let $x_0 \in X$. The constant sequence of measures $\mu_n = \delta_{x_0}$ satisfies the large deviation principle with the Dirac rate function of $x_0$, which is $0$ at $x_0$ and $\infty$ elsewhere.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
